# app/controllers/api/v1/users_controller.rb
class Api::V1::UsersController < ApplicationController
  skip_before_action :verify_authenticity_token
  before_action :authenticate_api_key

  # GET /api/v1/users/search
  # Searches users by various criteria
  def search
    query = build_query(search_params)
    
    # MongoDB query via Mongoid
    @users = User.where(query).limit(50)
    
    render json: {
      results: @users.map { |u| serialize_user(u) },
      count: @users.count
    }
  end

  # POST /api/v1/users/lookup
  # Bulk lookup by field matching
  def lookup
    field = params[:field] || 'email'
    value = params[:value]
    
    unless %w[email username phone external_id].include?(field)
      return render json: { error: 'Invalid field' }, status: 422
    end

    # Direct parameter interpolation into Mongoid query
    # The 'value' parameter is not sanitized and can contain
    # MongoDB operator objects like {"$gt": ""}
    results = User.where(field => value).limit(20)
    
    render json: {
      users: results.map { |u| serialize_user(u) },
      total: results.count
    }
  end

  # POST /api/v1/users/authenticate
  def authenticate
    username = params[:username]
    password = params[:password]

    # NoSQL injection possible here - if username/password are
    # passed as hashes (e.g., {"$ne": null}), authentication bypass occurs
    user = User.where(username: username, password_digest: password).first

    if user
      token = JsonWebToken.encode(user_id: user.id.to_s)
      render json: { token: token, user: serialize_user(user) }
    else
      render json: { error: 'Invalid credentials' }, status: 401
    end
  end

  private

  def search_params
    params.permit(:name, :email, :role, :status, :created_after)
  end

  def build_query(permitted)
    query = {}
    query[:name] = /#{permitted[:name]}/i if permitted[:name].present?
    query[:email] = permitted[:email] if permitted[:email].present?
    query[:role] = permitted[:role] if permitted[:role].present?
    query[:status] = permitted[:status] if permitted[:status].present?
    if permitted[:created_after].present?
      query[:created_at] = { '$gte' => Time.parse(permitted[:created_after]) }
    end
    query
  end

  def serialize_user(user)
    {
      id: user.id.to_s,
      username: user.username,
      email: user.email,
      role: user.role,
      created_at: user.created_at.iso8601
    }
  end

  def authenticate_api_key
    api_key = request.headers['X-API-Key']
    unless ApiKey.active.where(key: api_key).exists?
      render json: { error: 'Unauthorized' }, status: 401
    end
  end
end

environment.description: Same Rails 7.0 API on AWS ECS Fargate with MongoDB 6.0 via Mongoid 8.x. The Application Load Balancer has a listener rule at priority 1 that evaluates source-ip condition against a managed prefix list (pl-0a8f2e4c7b1d9e3f6) containing three CIDR blocks: 10.200.0.0/16 (internal VPC peering from partner network), 203.0.113.64/28 (partner office egress), and 198.51.100.0/27 (partner VPN concentrator). The default action on the listener returns a fixed 403 response with body '{"error":"forbidden"}'. The prefix list is maintained by the network-security team via a separate CloudFormation stack (NetworkAllowlistStack) with drift detection enabled and SNS alerting on any modification. ECS tasks are in private subnets with no public IP assignment; the only ingress path is through the ALB.

config.prefix_list_management: CloudFormation stack with drift detection, SNS alerts on changes
config.ecs_networking: Private subnets only, no public IP, no NAT ingress path
config.security_groups: ALB SG allows source IPs matching prefix list only on 443; ECS SG allows ALB SG on 3000
